_about: Owner order 2c: datasheet self-checks (kind B). Rules as data, each with an id and plain-English text. Pure arithmetic on the datasheet's own values - no standard, no model. Edit here, not in code; datasheet_checks.py reads this file.

fluid_phase._implied_by: R12 (#776, planner 2026-10-11 point 5a): when the phase is NOT stated, a fluid service that names one phase only (whole words) says which phase the sheet probably means. Used only to turn an item for the OTHER phase into an engineer's question - never a verdict, never 'does not apply'. A service naming both (e.g. 'water vapour') implies nothing.

specific_heat_ratio._plausible: R12 (#776, planner 2026-10-11 point 5b): k = Cp/Cv of a gas is above 1 and at most 5/3 (a monatomic ideal gas); a printed k outside this is a reading or entry error (a sheet printed 18). Above the range the value is an engineer's question and no calculation uses it; 'above 1' stays PSV-32's own check.

calc_units._about: R13 (#777): the units each API 520-I calculation converts its inputs from, as factors to one unit per table (key = the printed unit, lower case, no spaces, superscripts as digits). Temperature is converted in code (an offset, not a factor). A unit not listed is not guessed: the calculation is not run and says which unit it could not read.

_placeholders: Moved 2026-09-27 to app/blank_markers.py - the ONE list of not-provided markers every datasheet reader and these checks read (CLAUDE.md rule 8).

consistency.text: The design pressure should be at least the operating pressure.
The design temperature should be at least the operating temperature.
The test pressure should be higher than the design pressure.
The rated flow should not be below the minimum flow.
The rated flow should not be above the maximum flow.

checklists._about: #746: the review checklist per equipment type, in the one datasheet-checks engine. Each item: id, plain text, source {standard, clause} (required), a rule (required, compare, constant, percent_of, allowed, above_by: left >= right + the greater of a percent or an absolute margin, or calc: a named API 520-I calculation in code (R13) whose result the field is compared with), an optional condition {role, any} or a list of them that must all hold, a severity. Client standard items are written here in our own words (owner decision 2026-10-10); the local overlay <data_dir>/checklists/<type>.json stays for items not yet approved for the repo.

Pressure Safety Valve.note: DRAFT. API 520 Part I items: clause numbers are section headings found in the held copy; SAES-J-600 items: clause numbers and the check written in our own words from the held copy (owner decision 2026-10-10: client standard items go in this file, no verbatim text). The rule under each is an engineering reading, not checked line by line. Nothing here is binding until a client discipline engineer signs it off.

items.text: The set pressure is stated.
The maximum allowable working pressure is stated.
The design pressure is stated.
The maximum operating pressure is stated.
The relieving temperature is stated.
The allowable overpressure is stated.
The built-up back pressure is stated.
The superimposed back pressure is stated.
The cold differential test pressure is stated.
The required relieving capacity is stated.
The rated relieving capacity is stated.
The effective orifice area is stated.
The orifice designation is stated.
The inlet size is stated.
The outlet size is stated.
The valve type is stated as conventional, balanced (bellows) or pilot-operated.
The fluid is stated.
The fluid phase at relieving conditions is stated (gas or vapour, or liquid).
For gas or vapour relief, the molecular weight is stated.
For gas or vapour relief, the compressibility factor is stated.
For gas or vapour relief, the specific heat ratio (k) is stated.
For liquid relief, the density at relieving conditions is stated.
For liquid relief, the viscosity at relieving conditions is stated.
The set pressure does not exceed the maximum allowable working pressure.
The maximum allowable working pressure is at least the design pressure.
The maximum operating pressure leaves a margin below the set pressure (at most 90% of it).
For a fire case, the overpressure does not exceed 21%.
For a single device in a non-fire case, the overpressure does not exceed 10%.
For a conventional valve, the built-up back pressure does not exceed 10% of the set pressure.
The cold differential test pressure does not exceed the set pressure.
The rated relieving capacity is at least the required relieving capacity.
For gas or vapour relief, the specific heat ratio (k) is above 1.
For gas or vapour relief, the compressibility factor is above 0.
For gas or vapour relief, the molecular weight is above 0.
For gas or vapour relief, the selected effective orifice area is at least the required area calculated from the sheet's own inputs.
For gas or vapour relief, the required area the sheet states is at least the area calculated from the sheet's own inputs.
For liquid relief, the selected effective orifice area is at least the required area calculated from the sheet's own inputs.
For liquid relief, the required area the sheet states is at least the area calculated from the sheet's own inputs.
The inlet size is stated (the standard's minimum is 3/4 in threaded or 1 in flanged).
The inlet flange rating is at least ASME B16.5 Class 150.
The set pressure is above the maximum operating pressure by at least the greater of 10% or 100 kPa.
For a thermal relief valve, the set pressure does not exceed 110% of the maximum allowable pressure.
The governing relief case is stated (external fire is included where the codes require it).
The worst-case relieving rate the valve is sized for is stated.
The body material is stated (materials follow API 526 with the standard's exceptions).
The trim (nozzle and disc) material is stated.
In sour service, the spring material is stated (protected by bellows or a rupture disc, or crack-resistant).
For a bellows valve in sour service, the bellows are Alloy 625 or Alloy C-276.

Centrifugal Pump.note: DRAFT, needs the client engineer's approval. The fields an API 610 centrifugal pump datasheet carries, each written in our own words; every item asks only that the field is STATED. The clause numbers are NOT yet verified: the source clause names the datasheet annex and says the number is to be checked against the held copy (an engineer fills it through the local overlay, see scripts/pump_checklist_clauses.py). This checklist does NOT replace the standard's library requirements (governs: false): API 610 stays checked clause by clause beside it. "Stated" means a label of the field was found with a value, not that the value is the right kind: a bare "Casing", "Impeller", "Shaft", "Bearing" or "Speed" row (usually a type, not a material or the rated figure) and "Rated power" (often the driver's) are deliberately NOT read as these fields. Nothing here is binding until a client discipline engineer signs it off.
